katas.title: Sale form: one try/catch around the whole save flow

provenance.find: F1: two sequential writes behind one failure message.

defects.scenario: The sale row is written, then the follow-up pig-batch status write rejects; the user does what the alert says and re-submits.
defects.find: // One try/catch keeps the handler small: any failure in the save flow shows the same
defects.consequence: The retried add creates a second sale under a new id, doubling the quantity and revenue in every report. Nothing spans the two storage keys — saveList is one setItem per key — so the single "could not be saved, try again" message turns a partial failure into duplicated money (finding F1).

defects.scenario: The shipped screen awaits the pig-batch status write inside the same try as the sale write.
defects.consequence: If this second write rejects, the sale is already persisted under piggery_sales, yet the shared catch tells the user the sale could not be saved — a user who retries an add duplicates the sale (finding F1; the suggested direction is to report the two failures differently, or stop persisting a status calculations.ts:312 already derives).

tests.name: a batch-status failure after the sale persisted is not reported as an unsaved sale (finding F1)
tests.code: const saved = []; const alerts = []; const deps = { addSale: async (sale) => { saved.push(sale); }, updateSale: async () => { throw new Error('updateSale must not be called for a new sale'); }, updatePigBatch: async () => { throw new Error('disk full'); }, getBatchCurrentQuantity: () => 0, alert: (title, message) => { alerts.push({ title, message }); }, goBack: () => {}, }; const result = await mod.submitSale({ deps, sale: { id: 's1', quantity: 5 }, batch: { id: 'b1', status: 'active' }, existingSale: null, sales: [], mortalityRecords: [] }); assert.equal(saved.length, 1); assert.equal(result.saleSaved, true, 'the handler claims the persisted sale was not saved'); assert.equal(alerts.some((a) => a.message.includes('could not be saved')), false, 'the retry advice would duplicate the sale');

tests.name: a failed sale write is reported as unsaved with the retry alert
tests.code: const alerts = []; const deps = { addSale: async () => { throw new Error('storage offline'); }, updateSale: async () => {}, updatePigBatch: async () => {}, getBatchCurrentQuantity: () => 5, alert: (title, message) => alerts.push({ title, message }), goBack: () => {}, }; const result = await mod.submitSale({ deps, sale: { id: 's1' }, batch: { id: 'b1', status: 'active' }, existingSale: null, sales: [], mortalityRecords: [] }); assert.equal(result.saleSaved, false); assert.equal(alerts.some((a) => a.message.includes('could not be saved')), true);

tests.name: a sale that empties the batch marks it sold_out and navigates back
tests.code: const batches = []; let wentBack = false; const deps = { addSale: async () => {}, updateSale: async () => {}, updatePigBatch: async (b) => batches.push(b), getBatchCurrentQuantity: () => 0, alert: () => {}, goBack: () => { wentBack = true; }, }; const result = await mod.submitSale({ deps, sale: { id: 's1', quantity: 10 }, batch: { id: 'b1', status: 'active' }, existingSale: null, sales: [], mortalityRecords: [] }); assert.equal(result.saleSaved, true); assert.equal(result.batchClosed, true); assert.equal(batches[0].status, 'sold_out'); assert.equal(wentBack, true);

tests.name: editing an existing sale goes through updateSale, not addSale
tests.code: const updated = []; const deps = { addSale: async () => { throw new Error('addSale must not be called for an edit'); }, updateSale: async (sale) => updated.push(sale), updatePigBatch: async () => {}, getBatchCurrentQuantity: () => 3, alert: () => {}, goBack: () => {}, }; const result = await mod.submitSale({ deps, sale: { id: 's1', quantity: 2 }, batch: { id: 'b1', status: 'active' }, existingSale: { id: 's1' }, sales: [{ id: 's1', quantity: 1 }], mortalityRecords: [] }); assert.equal(result.saleSaved, true); assert.equal(updated.length, 1);

katas.title: Sale form: collapse error handling to one generic retry alert

provenance.find: the rejected promise lands in the bare `catch` at `SaleFormScreen.tsx:105`

defects.scenario: A sale is deleted on another screen, then a stale edit form for it submits.
defects.find: // Every failure ends the same way for the user, so one message covers them all.
defects.consequence: replaceRecordById's thrown "Record '<id>' was not found." is discarded by the bare catch: the user is told to try again, and retrying can never succeed. The specific message and the stale-identity signal are silently lost — exactly the step-6 trace, where 'try again' is misleading for this case.

defects.scenario: The shipped screen already funnels every rejection into one generic alert.
defects.find: Alert.alert("Save failed", "The sale could not be saved. Please try again.");
defects.consequence: In production, updateSale's rejection from collection.ts:4 lands in this bare catch: the stale-identity message is discarded and the user is told to retry an update that must fail forever (course step 6; step 7 adds that a repeated delete is idempotent but an update for an absent id must be surfaced).

tests.name: a stale update (record deleted elsewhere) is surfaced as a stale identity, not a retry (step 6)
tests.code: const alerts = []; const res = await mod.saveSaleUpdate({ sales: [{ id: 'other-sale' }], nextSale: { id: 'gone-id' }, persist: async () => {}, alert: (title, message) => alerts.push(message) }); assert.equal(res.stale, true, 'the stale-identity signal was swallowed'); assert.equal(alerts.some((m) => m.includes("Record 'gone-id' was not found.")), true, 'the specific message was discarded'); assert.equal(alerts.some((m) => m.includes('Please try again')), false, 'the user was told to retry an update that can never succeed');

tests.name: a transient persistence failure still suggests a retry
tests.code: const alerts = []; const res = await mod.saveSaleUpdate({ sales: [{ id: 's1' }], nextSale: { id: 's1' }, persist: async () => { throw new Error('storage offline'); }, alert: (title, message) => alerts.push(message) }); assert.equal(res.saved, false); assert.equal(res.stale, false); assert.equal(alerts.some((m) => m.includes('Please try again')), true);

tests.name: a successful update persists the replaced record
tests.code: let persisted = null; const res = await mod.saveSaleUpdate({ sales: [{ id: 's1', qty: 1 }], nextSale: { id: 's1', qty: 2 }, persist: async (next) => { persisted = next; }, alert: () => {} }); assert.equal(res.saved, true); assert.deepEqual(persisted, [{ id: 's1', qty: 2 }]);
